author: Leoboudv
source_description: This is an Albanian women's guibba or coat. It might date to the period around 1800 to 1850. This coat is a maroon velvet surcoat which is heavily ornamented with gold. This woman's coat has a fitted bodice and a full, calf-length skirt. The bodice and skirt are almost entirely covered with scrollwork embroidery, worked with metallic gold cord and metallic gold thread, except for a plain panel on each side of the bodice front and at the center of the bodice back. The garment, which is very stiff and heavy, is entirely interlined with animal skin, which supports the weight of the metallic embroidery. The coat today forms part of the permanent collection of the UBC Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver, Canada, where its museum catalogue number is 1185/1.

author: RBCt11
source_description: This is a pair of Skechers Energy 2 - Cruise Control model sneakers in US men's size 9 and Black/Charcoal color, in the original box. They were acquired in August 2024 from an eBay seller in like-new condition. The upper lid of the box (out of frame) displays a date stamp of "2004.12.27". The UPC number is 827443248093. The shoes bear the serial number 50165, and have a leather/synthetic upper. They bear two US patent numbers: D435162 (Shoe upper, 2000) and D454426 (Shoe bottom, 2002), both credited to Skechers U.S.A., Inc., II of Manhattan Beach, CA and Ralph Davis Wilson of Torrance, CA. They were manufactured in China. The Skechers Energy 2 line is evolved from the original Energy released in 1999, coming in multiple colors, styles, and sizes aimed at men, women, boys, and girls, featuring updated sole and upper designs. Like its predecessor, it was widely promoted in a celebrity marketing campaign that most prominently featured singer Britney Spears. It was also seen in posters featuring actor Robert Downey, Jr. and NBA player Rick Fox, and prominently worn by pop acts including BoA and AKB48. Skechers 4Wheelers roller skates were also made using this silhouette. Energy 2 designs were mostly produced in the early 2000s and phased out over the latter years of the decade and the early 2010s, as they were eclipsed by the newer D'Lites design. The Energy 2 highlights Skechers' embrace of trail running-inspired sneaker silhouettes in casual wear during the late 1990s and early 2000s and the wide popularity of both the brand and the trend, as its phase-out represents further evolution and trend changes. The original Energy was briefly revived in new colors and brand collaborations during the early 2020s revival of the chunky sneaker trend before being discontinued again,

author: Bill Abbott
source_description: Note mouse on top! Pretty hip for 1980... Mr. Belleville worked at Xerox PARC DSC_0663. Around that same time, my friend Jerry built a terminal for his home system that looked much like this. He had a Hall effect keyboard, a video monitor in a matching box. Each of the circuit cards he bought or designed and built plugged into an edge connector inside the monitor box. Each had DIP switches, and the setting guides, pinout and schematic were on folded pieces of paper stored between the cards. He ran out of space and gave it to me, I ran out of space and gave it to a co-worker 29 years ago. One side of the monitor box swung open, with a wing nut holding it shut when needed. The case was mahogany, and Jerry's paradigm was that a monitor was really a TV, and a TV in a mahogany box should have a Masonite back, so his did. Quotation [center] Belleville Personal Computer, Robert Belleville, US, ca. 1980 Robert Belleville designed this computer around the 8080 microprocessor. He included an audio processor with speakers, and made a scanner/printer to use with the system. Belleville's design was influenced by the Xerox Alto, which he had worked on. Speed: 2MHz Memory type: Semiconductor Memory width: 8bit Gift of Robert Belleville X2117.2001A [right] Ohio Scientific Model 600, Ohio Scientific, US, 1978 This Model 600 also called the Superboard II, was a single board computer with an integrated keyboard and 4K of static RAM. It was among the most affordable of early hobbyist computers, selling completed assembled for under $300. author: Dietmar Rabich
source_title: Dülmen, Kirchspiel, St.-Jakobus-Kirche, Chor und Altar -- 2022 -- 4184-8
source_description: Choirs and altar in the St Jacob’s Church (Karthaus) in Weddern hamlet, Kirchspiel, Dülmen , North Rhine-Westphalia , Germany The church belongs to the former Marienburg Charterhouse – the only Carthusian monastery in Westphalia. The order came to Weddern in 1476/77 after the knight Gerd von Keppel donated his castle to the order. The charterhouse was inhabited until 1803. Construction of the church itself began in 1477, but remained unfinished for a long time; the keystone in the western bay bears the date 1607. After the monastery was dissolved, the building remained standing and is now used as a parish and community center. The church is a late Gothic place of worship built of red brick. The building has a deliberately simple design: a single-nave hall with a vaulted ceiling, choir area, and characteristic tracery windows. A tower with an octagonal pointed roof and dormers characterizes the exterior appearance. In 1871/72, the church was expanded in the neo-Gothic style, with a crypt for the von Croÿ family added and the interior expanded. Particularly noteworthy is the old choir stalls, which probably originate from Cologne and date from around 1350. Also impressive is a Rococo grille from 1752, which visually separates the altar area from the church and is artistically decorated.

author: Dietmar Rabich
source_title: Heiligengrabe, Kloster Stift zum Heiligengrabe, Heiliggrabkapelle -- 2017 -- 0015-21
source_description: Altar of the Heiliggrabkapelle, Monastery Endowment of the Holy Grave, Heiligengrabe , Brandenburg , Germany The Holy Sepulchre Chapel belongs to the Cistercian convent, which was founded in 1287. As early as the 14th century, a “Holy Sepulchre” is mentioned at this location, which gave rise to the name Heiligengrabe (Holy Sepulchre). The present late Gothic chapel was consecrated in 1512 and built around 1520 on the site of earlier, more modest predecessor buildings. The building is a four-bay, star-vaulted hall structure made of brick with striking stepped gables. It is considered a masterpiece of North German brick Gothic architecture.

author: Dietmar Rabich
source_title: Heiligengrabe, Kloster Stift zum Heiligengrabe, Stiftskirche -- 2017 -- 9969
source_description: Altar in the Collegiate church, Monastery Endowment of the Holy Grave, Heiligengrabe , Brandenburg , Germany The monastery was founded in 1287 by the Ascanian Margrave Otto IV as a Cistercian convent and shortly afterwards occupied by nuns from the Neuendorf (Altmark) monastery. The collegiate church is part of the original monastery complex and was built as a single-nave hall church with ribbed vaulting and a polygonal choir, probably as early as the 14th or 15th century. Parts of the church were damaged during the Thirty Years’ War and later in a fire in 1719. After the fire in the 18th century, the interior layout was changed. Restoration of the roof structure and other components were important construction measures in 1890 and 1904. The redesigned gable was modeled on the neighboring Holy Sepulcher Chapel and was given a relief depicting the Jerusalem Cross. In the 20th century, despite political upheavals (the Weimar Republic, the Nazi era, and the GDR ), the church remained a place of Protestant community life.

As early as the 14th century, a “Holy Sepulchre” is mentioned at this location, which gave rise to the name Heiligengrabe (Holy Sepulchre). The present late Gothic chapel was consecrated in 1512 and built around 1520 on the site of earlier, more modest predecessor buildings. The building is a four-bay, star-vaulted hall structure made of brick with striking stepped gables. It is considered a masterpiece of North German brick Gothic architecture.

author: National Library NZ on The Commons
source_description: Maroon goatskin with ornate gold tooled frames on upper and lower covers. Armorial device of Alexander H. Turnbull in the centre. The bookbinding firm of Zaehnsdorf was founded in London in 1842 by Joseph Zaehnsdorf (1816-1886), an Austro-Hungarian craftsman-binder who learned his trade in Stuttgart and Vienna. While he was very successful, becoming ‘Bookbinder to the King of Hanover’ by 1861, it was under his son Joseph William Zaehnsdorf (1853-1930) that the firm was able to develop further and prosper. Joseph William did much to make known the principles of sound binding practice, and to increase the appreciation and knowledge of fine binding. He was the author of The art of bookbinding (1880) which became a standard textbook for apprentices, and he wrote a series of articles on amateur bookbinding in which he stated that the finishing or decorative side of bookbinding caused the most difficulty for the amateur. The firm was known for its high-quality workmanship and excelled in the retrospective binding popular in the 19th century. The firm’s most skilled craftsmen were reserved for the higher-quality work sometimes working from their own designs, and sometimes from designs produced by professional designers, both constructing their patterns from existing styles. This firm was at its height from the 1890s until the First World War, and it is during this period that Alexander Turnbull had many of his books bound. Purchased by Alexander H. Turnbull. Upper cover and spine of Richard Hakluyt, The principal navigations, voiages, traffiqves and discoueries of the English nation (Imprinted at London: by George Bishop, Ralph Newberie and Robert Barker, anno 1598-[1600]). qREng HAKL Prin 1598

author: KNOW MALTA by Peter Grima
source_description: POSTAL STAMP HISTORY NOTES. The first postal service dating back to around 4000 B.C was established in China and one thousand years later in Egypt. Letters were written on clay tablets. In 1661, Henry Bishop a British, was the first to use the Postmark, were it was known as the “Bishop Mark” which included the day and month the letter was posted. Rowland Hill, a British schoolmaster introduced the first adhesive stamp in 1837. Commemorative stamps were first issued in the U.S.A, in 1893 to Commemorate the voyage of Christopher Columbus. The stamps featured the images of Christopher Columbus. This set was issued to mark the 400-year anniversary of his journey to the New World. In 1874, the Universal Postal Union was established. A set of norms were introduced which included that the name of the country of origin be included on the stamp. MALTA STAMPS HISTORY It was during the Knights of Malta era, in the 18th century, that the postal system began in Malta, when the Knights use to sent letters from Malta to other European countries. When the French were ruling Malta, Napoleon, introduced the ink stamp which was marked with the word ( Malte ). In 1847, when Malta was a British colony, the first General Post Office was set up in Auberge de Castile in Valletta. To post letters for Malta and Gozo, one had to use the British stamps but these British stamps were stamped with an ink stamp marked A25 to show that the stamp was for Maltese inland postage only and had one standard rate. In 1860, when Malta was still a British colony, Malta issued it’s first stamp, a half penny yellow stamp. Issued in different perforations and shades, this stamp was used for Maltese inland postage only and was legal until 1885. Also until 1885, for overseas mail only British stamps had to be used.

source_description: www.noel.strasbourg.eu/ fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marché_de_Noel Les premières traces des marchés de Noël remontent au xive siècle en Allemagne et en Alsace, sous l'appellation « Marché de Saint Nicolas ». Le premier document relatant un marché de Noël est daté de 1434 sous le règne de Frédéric II de Saxe, évoquant un « Striezelmarkt » qui a eu lieu à Dresde le lundi précédent Noël. Plus tard, la Réforme a perpétué la tradition en le rebaptisant « Christkindelsmärik » (marché de l'Enfant Christ) pour lutter contre le culte des saints. Le marché de Noël de Strasbourg date de 1570, celui de Nuremberg de 1628. Au xixe siècle, le Christkindelsmärik se tenait au Frohnhof (place aux corvées) entre la cathédrale Notre-Dame de Strasbourg, le palais des Rohan de Strasbourg et le musée de l'Œuvre Notre-Dame (actuelle place du château) et avait lieu 8 jours avant Noël et jusqu'à la messe de minuit. Un important renouveau, considéré comme commercial, a eu lieu au milieu des années 1990. De nombreuses villes en Europe ont instauré leur propre marché de Noël avec des chalets et parfois des attractions. Strasbourg - Christkindelsmärik, place Broglie. Le plus ancien marché de Noël connu est celui de Strasbourg, qui était d'abord lié à saint Nicolas. En 1570 il a été déplacé à la veille de Noël le 24 décembre au soir avec des stands pour que les adultes, les parents puissent acheter des cadeaux aux enfants. En Alsace, la légende du saint Nicolas a traversé plusieurs siècles d'histoire. La légende raconte que trois petits enfants qui s'en allaient glaner aux champs se sont perdus dans la forêt. Recueillis par un boucher, celui-ci les découpe en petits morceaux et les dispose dans son saloir.
